There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. Can the World Support Ten New AGI Labs or Not? - We don’t know if we have enough new territory in AI that won’t be annexed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and other big labs. - New labs will need to meaningfully differentiate themselves to justify multi-billion dollar valuations. - It will be interesting to see if the world can support 10 research labs with 10 different variants of AI. 4. Why OpenAI Has the Largest Stock Based Comp of Any Company Ever? - If you are the CEO with zero shares, you do not worry about dilution. - Sam wants to build the greatest AI company. - If he needs to use equity for hiring & retention, it does not impact him as a shareholder. 5. You Can Identify a Top 0.1% Founder Without Ever Speaking to Them - I have had multiple billion-dollar exits from cold inbound deals. - I analyze the inbound & measure the quality of the founder. - It is not a leap of faith to imagine an AI could do a better job. 6. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 24.20% Remaining time 1:03 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on dilution here or a Twitter slash X dot AI investor rolling 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/eDd_6w5g Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/e62CEP_c Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/eqAudSGm My 8 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 6.05% Remaining time 1:04 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on Would you prefer to be a SpaceX investor taking 20% 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

author: Jason M. Lemkin
content: One thing that has really really accelerated the past 12 months is your partners competing with you. Expect the trend … to continue even more, and much faster, in 2026. The pace of the AI Age is leading to partners becoming competitors far, far faster than before. And often not even really thinking about it. They have no choice, as customer expectations for AI Agents are far higher than pre-AI apps. They want the AI Agent just to … get it done. And that often means crossing lines that used to separate B2B apps.

author: Jason M. Lemkin
content: 10 years ago, VC was optimized around $1B+ outcomes, for the most part. 5 years ago, VC was optimized around $10B+ outcomes. Today, VC is optimized around $100B+ outcomes. It’s exciting and bold and startups in the Age of AI grow faster than ever, by far Just understand what you are signing up for once you raise more than a few million.

author: SaaStr Ai
content: AI is poised to dramatically reshape the sales landscape. Email-based SDRs are facing near-extinction as AI can qualify leads instantly and effectively. While AEs might see a slower shift, a significant portion of their tasks will likely be augmented by AI. The rise of AI raises a crucial question: How will the sales profession evolve without traditional entry-level roles? The future favors those who can manage and collaborate with AI agents, possess deep product knowledge, and deliver genuine value. hashtag #AISales hashtag #SalesAutomation hashtag #FutureOfWork hashtag #SalesStrategy hashtag #Innovation

There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 54.44% Remaining time 1:05 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on Would you prefer to be a SpaceX investor taking 20% 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 12.10% Remaining time 1:05 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on Would you prefer to be a SpaceX investor taking 20% 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/eDd_6w5g Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/e62CEP_c Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/eqAudSGm My 8 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. To Do ElevenLabs At $11 Billion, You Have To Believe... - An $11B deal assumes a large, distributed customer base. - Not a few power users, but many real adopters paying. - The bet is that this proven trend keeps scaling for years. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 9.73% Remaining time 1:19 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on In the early stage, you're taking uncorrelated business 25 4 comments Like Comment Repost Send

Everyone Is Coming for Nvidia Now - Whether it’s buying from AMD, partnering with Broadcom, building your own chips… - NVIDIA’s numbers will still crush this year. - But we will likely see the competitive pressure start to build. 2. Why Did Nvidia Spend 20BN on Groq - NVIDIA has the world’s largest market cap, making a complex technical product, and charging a small number of customers 75% gross margins. - The last thing they need is someone who can make a vaguely comparable product – and that is Groq. - Buying up a competitor & eliminating that potential margin pressure for less than 1% of market cap & 20% annual free cash flow is worth it. 3. Can the World Support Ten New AGI Labs or Not? - We don’t know if we have enough new territory in AI that won’t be annexed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and other big labs. - New labs will need to meaningfully differentiate themselves to justify multi-billion dollar valuations. - It will be interesting to see if the world can support 10 research labs with 10 different variants of AI. 4. Why OpenAI Has the Largest Stock Based Comp of Any Company Ever? - If you are the CEO with zero shares, you do not worry about dilution. - Sam wants to build the greatest AI company. - If he needs to use equity for hiring & retention, it does not impact him as a shareholder. 5. You Can Identify a Top 0.1% Founder Without Ever Speaking to Them - I have had multiple billion-dollar exits from cold inbound deals. - I analyze the inbound & measure the quality of the founder. - It is not a leap of faith to imagine an AI could do a better job. 6. content: AI GTM agents don't figure out your go-to-market. They multiply what's already there. If your best rep runs a playbook that closes 10 deals a month, an AI agent runs that same playbook at 100x scale. If your team hasn't figured out what works yet — 10x times zero is still zero. Fix your playbook first. Deploy AI to run it second.

The "Supply Chain Risk" Weaponization The Department of Defense’s designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk is a massive escalation. While the immediate loss is a $200 million contract, the real "blast radius" is the potential to freeze the company out of the broader B2B economy. 2. Ambiguity is a B2B Deal Killer In enterprise sales, risk doesn't have to be certain to be fatal: it only has to be ambiguous. Anthropic’s already seeing deals cut in half or stalling because prospects fear government exposure. Competitors like OpenAI are reportedly capitalizing on this by positioning themselves as the "no-problem" alternative. 3. The Death of the Junior Employee We are entering a "world of the middle of the bell curve" regarding experience. Companies no longer want to spend 3–6 months training juniors when AI tools can provide instant, senior-level productivity. This isn't just a theory; Computer Science and Math graduates from solid state schools are already seeing "zero jobs" as companies stop hiring entry level jobs. 4. 24/7 Persistent AI is the Real Compute Driver Most people are currently using AI for episodic tasks (chatting, coding for an hour). But the next frontier is 24/7 persistent AI agents that watch, listen, and run in the background of your entire life. Moving from one agent to 50 agents running in parallel 24 hours a day will require orders of magnitude more compute than we have today. 5. The End of "Gentle Deceleration" In the public markets, the era of managing a polite, high-margin slowdown is dead. Investors are now brutally punishing any company that isn't actively re-accelerating. If you aren't showing CloudFlare-level acceleration or better, the public markets have effectively abandoned you. 6. Built-in Distribution vs. Product Velocity Wix is a fascinating lab experiment for the AI age. They have 6.1 million customers to cross-sell to, which helped their new AI product, Base 44, hit $100 million ARR. "Agent-Led Growth" is the New PLG The startups seeing "lines out the door" right now are the ones offering wholesale human replacement.. Founders should be building agents that are 90% better than humans in specific categories like GTM or support. When they can deliver that, the "budget magically comes out of nowhere". Real agents require custom training and data cleansing—complex work most firms aren't equipped to handle yet. 4. There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC …more Captions are auto generated Play 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

Everyone Is Coming for Nvidia Now - Whether it’s buying from AMD, partnering with Broadcom, building your own chips… - NVIDIA’s numbers will still crush this year. - But we will likely see the competitive pressure start to build. 2. Why Did Nvidia Spend 20BN on Groq - NVIDIA has the world’s largest market cap, making a complex technical product, and charging a small number of customers 75% gross margins. - The last thing they need is someone who can make a vaguely comparable product – and that is Groq. - Buying up a competitor & eliminating that potential margin pressure for less than 1% of market cap & 20% annual free cash flow is worth it. 3. Can the World Support Ten New AGI Labs or Not? - We don’t know if we have enough new territory in AI that won’t be annexed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and other big labs. - New labs will need to meaningfully differentiate themselves to justify multi-billion dollar valuations. - It will be interesting to see if the world can support 10 research labs with 10 different variants of AI. 4. Why OpenAI Has the Largest Stock Based Comp of Any Company Ever? - If you are the CEO with zero shares, you do not worry about dilution. - Sam wants to build the greatest AI company. - If he needs to use equity for hiring & retention, it does not impact him as a shareholder. 5. You Can Identify a Top 0.1% Founder Without Ever Speaking to Them - I have had multiple billion-dollar exits from cold inbound deals. - I analyze the inbound & measure the quality of the founder. - It is not a leap of faith to imagine an AI could do a better job. 6. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 48.39% Remaining time 1:04 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on Would you prefer to be a SpaceX investor taking 20% 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. The "Supply Chain Risk" Weaponization The Department of Defense’s designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk is a massive escalation. While the immediate loss is a $200 million contract, the real "blast radius" is the potential to freeze the company out of the broader B2B economy. 2. Ambiguity is a B2B Deal Killer In enterprise sales, risk doesn't have to be certain to be fatal: it only has to be ambiguous. Anthropic’s already seeing deals cut in half or stalling because prospects fear government exposure. Competitors like OpenAI are reportedly capitalizing on this by positioning themselves as the "no-problem" alternative. 3. The Death of the Junior Employee We are entering a "world of the middle of the bell curve" regarding experience. Companies no longer want to spend 3–6 months training juniors when AI tools can provide instant, senior-level productivity. This isn't just a theory; Computer Science and Math graduates from solid state schools are already seeing "zero jobs" as companies stop hiring entry level jobs. 4. 24/7 Persistent AI is the Real Compute Driver Most people are currently using AI for episodic tasks (chatting, coding for an hour). But the next frontier is 24/7 persistent AI agents that watch, listen, and run in the background of your entire life. Moving from one agent to 50 agents running in parallel 24 hours a day will require orders of magnitude more compute than we have today. 5. The End of "Gentle Deceleration" In the public markets, the era of managing a polite, high-margin slowdown is dead. Investors are now brutally punishing any company that isn't actively re-accelerating. If you aren't showing CloudFlare-level acceleration or better, the public markets have effectively abandoned you. 6. Built-in Distribution vs. Product Velocity Wix is a fascinating lab experiment for the AI age. They have 6.1 million customers to cross-sell to, which helped their new AI product, Base 44, hit $100 million ARR. However, if that $100M doesn’t exponentially compound to $600M+ quickly, it won't be enough to offset the 1-2% decline in their core legacy business. 7. "Agent-Led Growth" is the New PLG The startups seeing "lines out the door" right now are the ones offering wholesale human replacement.. Founders should be building agents that are 90% better than humans in specific categories like GTM or support. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. "Priced for Perfection" is a Dangerous Game When cybersecurity stocks dropped $20BN following an Anthropic feature release, it wasn't just about the tech; it was about the math. Rory notes that when companies trade at 16x–22x revenues, markets assume "perfection". In this environment, any "increase in tail risk" or a narrative shift leads to a brutal correction. 2. The "Fortnite" Circle is Shrinking for Software Jason uses a powerful analogy: Claude is like the game Fortnite: the safe territory for standalone software is shrinking as AI consumes more features. If your product can be "vibe coded" or exists purely as a feature within a browser or desktop, your surface area is under direct threat from foundation models. 3. Agents > "AI Dust" Incumbents struggle because they merely "sprinkle AI dust" on old analytics. To win, you must own the agent layer for your category. Real agents require custom training and data cleansing—complex work most firms aren't equipped to handle yet. 4. Great Productivity, Brutal Transition Productivity gains are "fricking awesome" long-term , but "Ghost GDP" warns of a "macroeconomic shock". If millions are displaced in months rather than decades, the pace of AI adoption may outstrip society's ability to adjust. 5. The "Toby Playbook" vs. Draconian Cuts Shopify has grown revenue by 50% to $12B without adding a single net headcount in three years. This is the "new normal." While healthy firms can hold headcount flat, Rory warns that highly levered, PE-backed SaaS companies may soon face "traumatic surgery": drastic 50% layoffs just to service their debt. 6. The Era of "Frankenstein" B2B Consolidation What happens to the $50M ARR unicorns with no acquirers? Jason predicts a "capitulation" where 5–20 startups are mashed together at "nominal prices" (1x–2x revenue) to create profitable, professionalized entities. It’s a "miserable way to consolidate debt," but it may be the only play left for many. 7. Momentum is the Only Play (For Now) In a state of total flux, value investing is out; momentum is in. Jason argues that in 2026, you bet on the winners (Palantir, Shopify, Figma) because "success begets success" and "gravitas" matters more than "bargain hunting" in an uncertain market. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC …more Activate to view larger image, Activate to view larger image, 18 2 comments Like Comment Repost Send

There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 5.97% Remaining time 1:06 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/eDd_6w5g Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/e62CEP_c Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/eqAudSGm My 8 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. To Do ElevenLabs At $11 Billion, You Have To Believe... - An $11B deal assumes a large, distributed customer base. - Not a few power users, but many real adopters paying. - The bet is that this proven trend keeps scaling for years. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 9.73% Remaining time 1:19 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on In the early stage, you're taking uncorrelated business 25 4 comments Like Comment Repost Send

Everyone Is Coming for Nvidia Now - Whether it’s buying from AMD, partnering with Broadcom, building your own chips… - NVIDIA’s numbers will still crush this year. - But we will likely see the competitive pressure start to build. 2. Why Did Nvidia Spend 20BN on Groq - NVIDIA has the world’s largest market cap, making a complex technical product, and charging a small number of customers 75% gross margins. - The last thing they need is someone who can make a vaguely comparable product – and that is Groq. - Buying up a competitor & eliminating that potential margin pressure for less than 1% of market cap & 20% annual free cash flow is worth it. 3. Can the World Support Ten New AGI Labs or Not? - We don’t know if we have enough new territory in AI that won’t be annexed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and other big labs. - New labs will need to meaningfully differentiate themselves to justify multi-billion dollar valuations. - It will be interesting to see if the world can support 10 research labs with 10 different variants of AI. 4. Why OpenAI Has the Largest Stock Based Comp of Any Company Ever? - If you are the CEO with zero shares, you do not worry about dilution. - Sam wants to build the greatest AI company. - If he needs to use equity for hiring & retention, it does not impact him as a shareholder. 5. You Can Identify a Top 0.1% Founder Without Ever Speaking to Them - I have had multiple billion-dollar exits from cold inbound deals. - I analyze the inbound & measure the quality of the founder. - It is not a leap of faith to imagine an AI could do a better job. 6. Why Navan Is a Screaming Buy Right Now! - 27% growth - Trading 4x ARR - Cash-flow positive - Profitable on non-GAAP basis. - The IPO timing & CFO stepping down means it is discounted right now. - It is probably 30-40% undervalued. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 7.28% Remaining time 0:54 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on 16 2 comments Like Comment Repost Send

Anthropic’s SuperBowl Ad Analysed - Consumer is Anthropic’s weakest sector. - They could have targeted the Super Bowl ad for engineers. - But they went for a cheap dig & advertised their worst product. 2. The AI Budget Revenue Stack & Why It's Not a Zero-Sum Game - AI revenue can be the same dollar showing up in multiple layers. - When a customer pays Atlassian, they pay AWS first, then AWS pays Anthropic. - Big headline numbers hide how much is shared across the stack. 3. The Idea That SaaS is Dead as a Category is BS - SaaS is not dead; it is alive and kicking. - Not all companies will make it in the next 5-10 years, but there will be companies that will continue to prosper. - It’s the history of the tech industry. 4. We Have to Give Up on TAM - We have to let the revenue numbers show us the path to TAM. - Harvey went from $200M to $600M ARR. - They showed us the money to TAM. 5. Why Customer Support Is a Trojan Horse - When the customer support agent becomes the main agent you’re working with, it understands the context of your business. - You can start using it for sales help or research. - It becomes a trojan horse to do everything else. 6. You Can't Get Fired for Buying the Winner - No one is trying to be contrarian anymore; they are all piling on winners. - You can’t get fired for putting money with a 1x preference. - It’s the VC equivalent of “You can’t get fired for buying IBM” hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 19.57% Remaining time 0:36 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on to me. Just tech. - SpaceX Completes $1.25TRN XAI Acquisition - The 2026 SaaS Massacre: Public Market Collapse - Microsoft's $360 Billion Market Cap Loss - NVIDIA's $100BN Investment Dispute with OpenAI - Waymo Raises $16 Billion at a $110 Billion Valuation Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/e-ZqhrF7 Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/eT28C6vp Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/e2DAq5pa My 6 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 18.15% Remaining time 1:06 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on Would you prefer to be a SpaceX investor taking 20% 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

Everyone Is Coming for Nvidia Now - Whether it’s buying from AMD, partnering with Broadcom, building your own chips… - NVIDIA’s numbers will still crush this year. - But we will likely see the competitive pressure start to build. 2. Why Did Nvidia Spend 20BN on Groq - NVIDIA has the world’s largest market cap, making a complex technical product, and charging a small number of customers 75% gross margins. - The last thing they need is someone who can make a vaguely comparable product – and that is Groq. - Buying up a competitor & eliminating that potential margin pressure for less than 1% of market cap & 20% annual free cash flow is worth it. 3. Can the World Support Ten New AGI Labs or Not? - We don’t know if we have enough new territory in AI that won’t be annexed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and other big labs. - New labs will need to meaningfully differentiate themselves to justify multi-billion dollar valuations. - It will be interesting to see if the world can support 10 research labs with 10 different variants of AI. 4. Why OpenAI Has the Largest Stock Based Comp of Any Company Ever? - If you are the CEO with zero shares, you do not worry about dilution. - Sam wants to build the greatest AI company. - If he needs to use equity for hiring & retention, it does not impact him as a shareholder. 5. You Can Identify a Top 0.1% Founder Without Ever Speaking to Them - I have had multiple billion-dollar exits from cold inbound deals. - I analyze the inbound & measure the quality of the founder. - It is not a leap of faith to imagine an AI could do a better job. 6. Why Navan Is a Screaming Buy Right Now! - 27% growth - Trading 4x ARR - Cash-flow positive - Profitable on non-GAAP basis. - The IPO timing & CFO stepping down means it is discounted right now. - It is probably 30-40% undervalued. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 29.14% Remaining time 0:52 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on Everyone's coming for NVIDIA now. No politics. Just tech. - Anthropic’s $10BN Fundraise… Has Claude Beaten Cursor? - a16z’s $15BN Fundraise: Is VC Go Big or Go Home in 2026? - How OpenAI Could Go to Zero? - Is ElevenLabs at $11BN a Buy? Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/eDd_6w5g Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/e62CEP_c Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/eqAudSGm My 8 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. To Do ElevenLabs At $11 Billion, You Have To Believe... - An $11B deal assumes a large, distributed customer base. - Not a few power users, but many real adopters paying. - The bet is that this proven trend keeps scaling for years. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 9.73% Remaining time 1:18 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on risk, and in the late stage you're taking 100% correlated 25 4 comments Like Comment Repost Send

Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/eDd_6w5g Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/e62CEP_c Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/eqAudSGm My 8 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. To Do ElevenLabs At $11 Billion, You Have To Believe... - An $11B deal assumes a large, distributed customer base. - Not a few power users, but many real adopters paying. - The bet is that this proven trend keeps scaling for years. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 9.73% Remaining time 1:17 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on risk, and in the late stage you're taking 100% correlated 25 4 comments Like Comment Repost Send

There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. Is the Elon Premium on SpaceX Justified? - SpaceX had ~$15BN revenue in ‘24 and ~$18BN in ‘25, growing ~30%. - The market is valuing it at ~50x run-rate revenue. - It feels like 80% of the value is the Elon premium, and 20% of the value is the actual business. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 18.15% Remaining time 1:05 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on Would you prefer to be a SpaceX investor taking 20% 19 1 comment 2 reposts Like Comment Repost Send

There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Dispersion Between Old and Low Growth and New and High Growth in Terms of Valuation Has Never Been More - We are seeing a heightened dispersion: low-growth companies are at 3x, and high-growth companies are at 50-100x. - New & exciting companies are getting insane multiples, while old & boring companies are going down. - A lot of software companies are moving to old & boring. 5. Why the $100BN Paid for Waymo Is Actually Cheap - Tesla’s market cap is ~$1.2TN. Assume the $100BN car business is valued at 2x revenue = $200BN. - That leaves ~$1TN for non-car assets. - Assuming a 50/50 split between Optimus & self-driving = ~$500BN each. - Waymo’s $100BN looks cheap compared to Tesla’s $500BN. 6. The "Supply Chain Risk" Weaponization The Department of Defense’s designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk is a massive escalation. While the immediate loss is a $200 million contract, the real "blast radius" is the potential to freeze the company out of the broader B2B economy. 2. Ambiguity is a B2B Deal Killer In enterprise sales, risk doesn't have to be certain to be fatal: it only has to be ambiguous. Anthropic’s already seeing deals cut in half or stalling because prospects fear government exposure. Competitors like OpenAI are reportedly capitalizing on this by positioning themselves as the "no-problem" alternative. 3. The Death of the Junior Employee We are entering a "world of the middle of the bell curve" regarding experience. Companies no longer want to spend 3–6 months training juniors when AI tools can provide instant, senior-level productivity. This isn't just a theory; Computer Science and Math graduates from solid state schools are already seeing "zero jobs" as companies stop hiring entry level jobs. 4. 24/7 Persistent AI is the Real Compute Driver Most people are currently using AI for episodic tasks (chatting, coding for an hour). But the next frontier is 24/7 persistent AI agents that watch, listen, and run in the background of your entire life. Moving from one agent to 50 agents running in parallel 24 hours a day will require orders of magnitude more compute than we have today. 5. The End of "Gentle Deceleration" In the public markets, the era of managing a polite, high-margin slowdown is dead. Investors are now brutally punishing any company that isn't actively re-accelerating. If you aren't showing CloudFlare-level acceleration or better, the public markets have effectively abandoned you. 6. Built-in Distribution vs. Product Velocity Wix is a fascinating lab experiment for the AI age. They have 6.1 million customers to cross-sell to, which helped their new AI product, Base 44, hit $100 million ARR. However, if that $100M doesn’t exponentially compound to $600M+ quickly, it won't be enough to offset the 1-2% decline in their core legacy business. 7. "Agent-Led Growth" is the New PLG The startups seeing "lines out the door" right now are the ones offering wholesale human replacement.. Founders should be building agents that are 90% better than humans in specific categories like GTM or support. When they can deliver that, the "budget magically comes out of nowhere". Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/eDd_6w5g Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/e62CEP_c Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/eqAudSGm My 8 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. To Do ElevenLabs At $11 Billion, You Have To Believe... - An $11B deal assumes a large, distributed customer base. - Not a few power users, but many real adopters paying. - The bet is that this proven trend keeps scaling for years. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC …more Captions are auto generated Play 25 4 comments Like Comment Repost Send

"Priced for Perfection" is a Dangerous Game When cybersecurity stocks dropped $20BN following an Anthropic feature release, it wasn't just about the tech; it was about the math. Rory notes that when companies trade at 16x–22x revenues, markets assume "perfection". In this environment, any "increase in tail risk" or a narrative shift leads to a brutal correction. 2. The "Fortnite" Circle is Shrinking for Software Jason uses a powerful analogy: Claude is like the game Fortnite: the safe territory for standalone software is shrinking as AI consumes more features. If your product can be "vibe coded" or exists purely as a feature within a browser or desktop, your surface area is under direct threat from foundation models. 3. Agents > "AI Dust" Incumbents struggle because they merely "sprinkle AI dust" on old analytics. To win, you must own the agent layer for your category. Real agents require custom training and data cleansing—complex work most firms aren't equipped to handle yet. 4. Great Productivity, Brutal Transition Productivity gains are "fricking awesome" long-term , but "Ghost GDP" warns of a "macroeconomic shock". If millions are displaced in months rather than decades, the pace of AI adoption may outstrip society's ability to adjust. 5. The "Toby Playbook" vs. Draconian Cuts Shopify has grown revenue by 50% to $12B without adding a single net headcount in three years. This is the "new normal." While healthy firms can hold headcount flat, Rory warns that highly levered, PE-backed SaaS companies may soon face "traumatic surgery": drastic 50% layoffs just to service their debt. 6. The Era of "Frankenstein" B2B Consolidation What happens to the $50M ARR unicorns with no acquirers? Jason predicts a "capitulation" where 5–20 startups are mashed together at "nominal prices" (1x–2x revenue) to create profitable, professionalized entities. It’s a "miserable way to consolidate debt," but it may be the only play left for many. 7. Momentum is the Only Play (For Now) In a state of total flux, value investing is out; momentum is in. Jason argues that in 2026, you bet on the winners (Palantir, Shopify, Figma) because "success begets success" and "gravitas" matters more than "bargain hunting" in an uncertain market. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Activate to view larger image, Activate to view larger image, 18 2 comments Like Comment Repost Send

Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. Rory notes that when companies trade at 16x–22x revenues, markets assume "perfection". In this environment, any "increase in tail risk" or a narrative shift leads to a brutal correction. 2. The "Fortnite" Circle is Shrinking for Software Jason uses a powerful analogy: Claude is like the game Fortnite: the safe territory for standalone software is shrinking as AI consumes more features. If your product can be "vibe coded" or exists purely as a feature within a browser or desktop, your surface area is under direct threat from foundation models. 3. Agents > "AI Dust" Incumbents struggle because they merely "sprinkle AI dust" on old analytics. To win, you must own the agent layer for your category. Real agents require custom training and data cleansing—complex work most firms aren't equipped to handle yet. 4. Great Productivity, Brutal Transition Productivity gains are "fricking awesome" long-term , but "Ghost GDP" warns of a "macroeconomic shock". If millions are displaced in months rather than decades, the pace of AI adoption may outstrip society's ability to adjust. 5. The "Toby Playbook" vs. Draconian Cuts Shopify has grown revenue by 50% to $12B without adding a single net headcount in three years. This is the "new normal." While healthy firms can hold headcount flat, Rory warns that highly levered, PE-backed SaaS companies may soon face "traumatic surgery": drastic 50% layoffs just to service their debt. 6. The Era of "Frankenstein" B2B Consolidation What happens to the $50M ARR unicorns with no acquirers? Jason predicts a "capitulation" where 5–20 startups are mashed together at "nominal prices" (1x–2x revenue) to create profitable, professionalized entities. It’s a "miserable way to consolidate debt," but it may be the only play left for many. 7. Momentum is the Only Play (For Now) In a state of total flux, value investing is out; momentum is in. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. There Are Only Two Types of Companies - Private companies: either hypergrowth or effectively unfundable in today’s market. - Public companies: only accelerating businesses matter, not ones that are slowing. - If you’re not clearly improving fast, it’s not worth the time. 2. The Shift From Being Valued on Revenue Multiples to Free Cash Flow - When investors are comparing you to steady industries, it’s a huge valuation reset. - It will take years of flat stock price and reasonable growth before you can be worth 10-15x FCF. - You don’t see a bottom until these stocks trade at free cash flow multiples net of dilution. 3. NVIDIA Would Have to Bail Out OpenAI - If NVIDIA can afford it, they have to bail out OpenAI if they stumble. - Other competitors like Anthropic are already diversifying to TPUs and AWS. - OpenAI is too big to fail. 4. Spotify 👉 https://lnkd.in/eDd_6w5g Youtube 👉 https://lnkd.in/e62CEP_c Apple Podcasts 👉 https://lnkd.in/eqAudSGm My 8 takeaways with Jason Lemkin and Rory O'Driscoll 👇 1. How a16z Do 3x On Their New Fund Size? - a16z raised $15B, about 20% of total venture capital raised. - Exits hit roughly $300B this year, making 3x returns mathematically possible. - With IPOs coming, the market may absorb big funds without breaking. 2. Founders Do Not Care If A Firm Can Invest More At Every Stage - Founders don’t really care if a VC can fund every stage. - They care about help, capital, and terms right now. - Winning great early deals matters more than future promises. 3. Adding A Growth Fund Is A Very Strategic Addition To Small Funds. - Adding a late-stage fund can raise a firm’s profile with founders. - It meaningfully boosts partner economics if executed well. - The risk is misplaying growth and damaging the core franchise. 4. How a16z’s Strategy is Genius & What it Means For The Rest Of Us - a16z split into $BN boutique funds to avoid quality decay. - The real edge is brand power and late-stage cleanup capital. - Smaller funds can win by being earlier and non-consensus. 5. Is The Market So Efficient That Every Great Company Has To Go Through Yc Or Andreessen? - Can $10B companies still be found outside YC and Andreessen? - If not, venture becomes access, signaling, and small checks. - Real alpha depends on true discovery still existing. 6. Business Risk vs Valuation Risk - Early-stage takes uncorrelated business risk. - Late-stage takes highly correlated valuation risk. - When markets dislocate, late-stage pain hits everyone together. 7. Why The Wealth Tax In California Being Proposed Is Much Worse Than It Seems - This wealth tax is a Trojan horse, not a one-time hit. - The real plan is an annual tax on $25–$50M of paper wealth. - It risks pushing founders to leave long before liquidity. 8. To Do ElevenLabs At $11 Billion, You Have To Believe... - An $11B deal assumes a large, distributed customer base. - Not a few power users, but many real adopters paying. - The bet is that this proven trend keeps scaling for years. hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 44.04% Remaining time 1:18 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on In the early stage, you're taking uncorrelated business 25 4 comments Like Comment Repost Send

You Can't Get Fired for Buying the Winner - No one is trying to be contrarian anymore; they are all piling on winners. - You can’t get fired for putting money with a 1x preference. - It’s the VC equivalent of “You can’t get fired for buying IBM” hashtag #founder hashtag #funding hashtag #business hashtag #investing hashtag #vc hashtag #entrepreneur hashtag #startup hashtag #investment hashtag #20VC Captions are auto generated Play Loaded: 88.71% Remaining time 0:37 1x Playback speed Turn closed captions off Unmute Turn fullscreen on to me. Can the World Support Ten New AGI Labs or Not? - We don’t know if we have enough new territory in AI that won’t be annexed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and other big labs. - New labs will need to meaningfully differentiate themselves to justify multi-billion dollar valuations. - It will be interesting to see if the world can support 10 research labs with 10 different variants of AI. 4. Can the World Support Ten New AGI Labs or Not? - We don’t know if we have enough new territory in AI that won’t be annexed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and other big labs. - New labs will need to meaningfully differentiate themselves to justify multi-billion dollar valuations. - It will be interesting to see if the world can support 10 research labs with 10 different variants of AI. 4.
